(1) A staged runner that validates the whole machine on near-free hardware before any H200 is touched, plus swappable recipe files so a failed H200 attempt costs one file change rather than a redesign. (2) A checkpoint mirror in S3 so a retry never re-downloads 151 GB from HuggingFace, and a results collector that pulls run output from S3 into results/ in the exact JSON schema scripts/compare-results.sh already parses. (3) Documentation: a runbook with copy-pasteable commands and honest per-stage costs, a postmortem of the failed run, and corrections to the factual errors this investigation found in README.md. steps: Create scripts/recipes/ holding one env file per candidate SGLang configuration, each a plain `KEY=value` file that launch-bench-ec2.sh sources and folds into the user-data env prelude. Write three, all with `--speculative-algorithm` spelled correctly (NOT `--speculative-algo`, which is what scripts/run-benchmark.sh currently emits and is a likely hard startup failure): (a) h200-tp4-fp4-eagle.env - model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash, tp=4, EAGLE low-latency preset steps=3 / eagle-topk=1 / draft-tokens=4, TP-only with DP-attention explicitly OFF, and the W4A16 Marlin MoE runner path the cookbook prescribes for Hopper FP4; (b) h200-tp4-fp8-eagle.env - model sgl-project/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-FP8 (294.1 GB / 273.9 GiB, the repackaged FP8 weights the cookbook says are H100/H200 only and which unlock DP-attention + DeepEP), same EAGLE preset; (c) h200-tp4-dspark-0731.env - model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 with `--speculative-algorithm DSPARK` and NO --speculative-num-steps / --speculative-eagle-topk / --speculative-num-draft-tokens, because the cookbook states SGLang reads the DSpark shape from the checkpoint and that this variant is verified on 4xH200. Each file must carry a header comment citing its upstream source and stating the exact checkpoint byte size so the disk guard has a value to check against. Do not invent flags: any flag you cannot find in the cookbook or `sglang serve --help` documentation must be left out and noted in findings.

Create scripts/run-staged.sh, the progressive driver, house style as usual, with --stage taking one of: preflight, plumbing, gpu-smoke, full. Stage preflight = scripts/preflight.sh only, zero cost, no CONFIRM_SPEND needed. Stage plumbing = c5d.large spot (2 vCPU, 1 x 50 GB NVMe instance store, no GPU, a couple of cents per hour) running the real bench-bootstrap.sh with a tiny stand-in payload, which exercises single-disk instance-store mount, S3 log and result streaming, CloudWatch heartbeat, spot-interruption polling, the wall-clock watchdog and self-termination on genuine EC2 metal. Stage gpu-smoke = g6e.xlarge spot (1 x L40S, 1 x 250 GB NVMe, well under a dollar per hour) running the same bootstrap with a small model to exercise docker --gpus all, the NVIDIA runtime, nvidia-smi telemetry, SGLang server startup and a short bench_serving; note README section 9.1 records that SGLang v0.5.12 flashinfer fails on SM 7.5 Turing with KeyError 'sm_75', so use L40S (SM 89) and not a T4 instance. Stage full = p5en.48xlarge spot per the selected recipe. Every stage after preflight must refuse to run without CONFIRM_SPEND=yes and must print its own cost estimate first. Default with no --stage is preflight.

run-staged.sh must also write a stage ledger to results/stage-ledger.json (gitignored) recording for each attempted stage: stage name, run id, instance type, start and end time, instance id, exit status, and the S3 prefix, so a later session can see at a glance which stages have passed and which recipe was last tried. Iteration state must live in the repo and in S3, never only in a chat session - that is the specific failure being engineered out.

Create scripts/mirror-checkpoint.sh: mirrors a HuggingFace repo into s3://<results-bucket>/checkpoints/<repo-id>/ so retries pull the weights in-region instead of re-downloading from HuggingFace. It must resolve the exact byte total via the HF API first (the same query FEAT-001 preflight uses), print the resulting S3 storage cost per month (S3 Standard is about $0.023/GB-month, so ~$3.7/mo for the 159.6 GB FP4 checkpoint and ~$6.8/mo for the 294.1 GB FP8 one) and require confirmation before uploading, support resume via `aws s3 sync`, and verify completeness by comparing the object count and total size against the HF manifest. Document that the mirror is what turns a failed H200 attempt from a 151 GB re-download into a fast in-region sync, and that CHECKPOINT_S3_URI in the recipe files is what activates it. Note in the runbook that the cheapest way to populate the mirror is from the benchmark instance itself during a full run (it already has the weights on NVMe), not from the sandbox.

Create scripts/collect-results.sh: given a RUN_ID, downloads s3://<bucket>/runs/<RUN_ID>/ into a local scratch dir, parses the two bench_serving outputs, and writes results/${INSTANCE_TYPE//./-}_tp${TP_SIZE}_${TIMESTAMP}.json plus the matching _summary.txt using the SAME schema scripts/run-benchmark.sh produces, because scripts/compare-results.sh reads exactly metadata.{instance_type,tp_size,region,timestamp} and, for each of custom_benchmark and official_benchmark, .config.{input_tokens,output_tokens,num_prompts,max_concurrency}, .results.* and .pass. Reuse run-benchmark.sh's threshold logic (TPOT P50 <= 4.5 ms, TTFT P50 <= 1700 ms) and its tolerant key lookups (tpot_p50_ms or inter_token_latency_p50_ms, ttft_p50_ms or time_to_first_token_p50_ms, etc). Verify the shape by feeding collect-results.sh a synthetic fixture under tests/fixtures/ and then running scripts/compare-results.sh against a temp results dir, asserting the table shows real numbers rather than N/A - add that as a case in tests/run-tests.sh. Also confirm and handle what `python3 -m sglang.bench_serving --output-file` actually writes: recent SGLang versions append one JSON object per line (JSONL), which `json.load` cannot parse, so the collector must handle the JSONL form and read the last record; state in findings which form you implemented against and why.

=== SGLANG FLAGS: WHAT I CONFIRMED vs WHAT I DELIBERATELY LEFT OUT ===
Sources: the cookbook (README section 10's 上游权威, fetched in full this session) and the upstream server_arguments reference https://docs.sglang.ai/advanced_features/server_arguments.html (also fetched, it is the published `sglang serve --help`).
CONFIRMED AND USED:
- `--speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-num-steps 3 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4` - all four spellings appear verbatim in the cookbook's AMD MTP note, and all four are in the server_arguments speculative table. This is the low-latency preset (steps=3, draft-tokens=4) the cookbook prescribes for the original Flash checkpoint.
- `--speculative-algorithm DSPARK` with NO steps/topk/draft-tokens and NO --speculative-draft-model-path - cookbook 3.4 states this explicitly ('SGLang reads the DSpark shape from the checkpoint').
- `--moe-runner-backend marlin` - the option value `marlin` is in the server_arguments --moe-runner-backend list, and the cookbook's Hopper note says the original FP4 path 'apply[s] the W4A16 MoE kernels (Marlin)'. Used in both FP4 recipes.
- `--dp-size N --enable-dp-attention` - both documented; the doc for --enable-dp-attention says 'The dp size should be equal to the tp size', which is why the FP8 recipe uses --dp-size 4 with tp 4. Only in the FP8 recipe, because the cookbook says the FP4/Marlin path is TP-only.
- `--enable-metrics`, `--mem-fraction-static`, `--trust-remote-code` - all documented.
LEFT OUT ON PURPOSE (each noted in the recipe comments):
- `--fp4-gemm-backend marlin`: real and documented ('weight-only W4A16 fallback for SM80-SM90'), but its `auto` ALREADY resolves to marlin on SM80-SM90 per the same doc, so specifying both it and --moe-runner-backend risks two knobs fighting. Left at auto, documented in the FP4 recipe header.
- DeepEP (`--moe-a2a-backend deepep --deepep-mode auto --ep-size 4 --max-running-requests 8`): present but COMMENTED OUT in the FP8 recipe. Reason: the cookbook attaches a hard constraint (max-running-requests x MTP_draft_tokens <= SGLANG_DEEPEP_NUM_MAX_DISPATCH_TOKENS_PER_RANK, violating it blows the dispatch buffer at deep_ep.cpp:1105) and I have no verified value for that env var. Also that env var must reach INSIDE the container and bench-bootstrap.sh has no generic env passthrough to `docker run` - I recorded that limitation in the recipe comment rather than pretending an `export` in the recipe would work.
- SM90 FP8 MegaMoE (`--moe-a2a-backend megamoe` + SGLANG_DSV4_FP4_EXPERTS=0): commented out. Cookbook marks it Experimental, it needs a sgl-deep-gemm build with SM90 FP8 MegaMoE support, and it targets long-context/large-decode throughput while our acceptance target is single-concurrency latency.
- `--speculative-dspark-block-size N`: omitted. Cookbook says the checkpoint default (5 proposed tokens) IS the verified value; sweeping 1..5 is a later tuning step.
- `--cuda-graph-max-bs-decode` / `--max-running-requests`: omitted from recipes. run-benchmark.sh passes `--cuda-graph-max-bs 64`, which the docs list as a deprecated alias; with max-concurrency=1 a bs-64 decode graph only lengthens the 10-15 min cold start. Left at defaults.
DISCREPANCY WORTH KNOWING: `DSPARK` is NOT in the server_arguments --speculative-algorithm option list (which stops at EAGLE, EAGLE3, NEXTN, STANDALONE, NGRAM), only in the V4 cookbook. So the DSpark recipe MUST run on lmsysorg/sglang:latest (cookbook says v0.5.16 is current); pinning an older tag will fail. All three recipes therefore set SGLANG_IMAGE=lmsysorg/sglang:latest, per the cookbook's 'a single image covers B200/B300/GB200/GB300/H100/H200'.
LAUNCH CLI: the cookbook's command panel uses `sglang serve`; run-benchmark.sh and bench-bootstrap.sh use `python3 -m sglang.launch_server`. I kept the latter as the active value in all three recipes (works on old and new images, lower failure surface) with the `sglang serve` line present-but-commented and a runbook note to validate a swap on the $0.3 gpu-smoke stage first. Also noted: `--tp` and `--dp` are not documented spellings (the documented ones are --tp-size/--tensor-parallel-size and --dp-size/--data-parallel-size); `--tp` only works via argparse prefix matching. I left bench-bootstrap.sh's `--tp` alone (not my file to churn) but used `--dp-size` in both the FP8 recipe and the run-benchmark.sh fix.

=== WHAT `sglang.bench_serving --output-file` ACTUALLY WRITES ===
Verified against upstream source, not guessed: python/sglang/bench_serving.py is now a deprecation shim and the implementation lives in python/sglang/benchmark/serving.py. At its end: `with open(output_file_name, "a") as file: file.write(json.dumps(result_for_dump) + "\n")`. So it is APPEND-mode JSONL - one JSON object per line, and re-running against the same path adds lines rather than replacing. `json.load` raises on a multi-line file. The default filename even ends in .jsonl.
Key names from the same source (there is no `*_p50_*` key anywhere; median_* IS the P50): mean/median/std/p90/p95/p99 x {ttft_ms, tpot_ms, itl_ms, e2e_latency_ms}, plus output_throughput, request_throughput, concurrency, accept_length, completed, duration.
COLLECTOR IMPLEMENTATION: load_bench() first tries whole-file json.loads (so a hand-written single-object fixture still works), then falls back to line-by-line parsing and takes the LAST valid record, and it reports which form it saw in both the summary and metadata.bench_output_form. normalize() then writes the canonical keys compare-results.sh reads (tpot_p50_ms <- median_tpot_ms, tpot_p95_ms <- p95_tpot_ms, ttft_p50_ms <- median_ttft_ms, ttft_p95_ms <- p95_ttft_ms, e2e_latency_p50_ms <- median_e2e_latency_ms, output_throughput_tok_per_s <- output_throughput) with the older/alias names as fallbacks, while KEEPING every raw key so nothing is lost. The same JSONL loader and normalizer were retrofitted into run-benchmark.sh (both its parse_and_judge and its result-merge block) - without the normalizer, run-benchmark.sh's own results would have shown N/A in compare-results.sh too, because its original lookups (tpot_p50_ms / inter_token_latency_p50_ms) match no real bench_serving key.
The fixture proves the last-record rule: bench_custom_*.json has TWO lines and the FIRST is deliberately failing (median_tpot_ms 9.99 > 4.5). Reading the first record flips case 13 to FAIL.

=== ONE REAL BUG FOUND IN EXISTING CODE (fixed, 3-line change) ===
scripts/compare-results.sh took a results dir as $1 but its python heredoc read `os.environ.get("RESULTS_DIR", sys.argv[1] ...)`, and RESULTS_DIR was a plain shell variable, never exported, while the heredoc gets no argv. So the directory argument was SILENTLY IGNORED and the script always globbed ./results relative to cwd - `compare-results.sh /tmp/rtest` printed '找到 1 个结果文件' followed by '没有可用的测试结果'. Without fixing this, acceptance criterion 3 is unreachable. Fix: `export RESULTS_DIR` plus a comment explaining why. Case 13 asserts the absence of '没有可用的测试结果' so this cannot silently regress.

=== RECOMMENDED RECIPE ORDER FOR THE FIRST REAL ATTEMPT: A -> C -> B ===
A = h200-tp4-fp4-eagle.env FIRST. It is simultaneously the smallest download (159.6 GB), the official instruct checkpoint, the Hopper path the cookbook spells out (W4A16 Marlin), and the algorithm behind README 12.3's single 已验证 configuration (H200 tp=4 + EAGLE 3/1/4, ~266 tok/s = TPOT ~3.76 ms). Smallest failure surface, closest to the number we are trying to reproduce.
C = h200-tp4-dspark-0731.env SECOND. Relative to A it changes exactly ONE variable, the speculative-decoding path, and the cookbook marks the 0731 checkpoint verified on 4xH200 specifically. Only +7 GB of weights. If A dies at server startup, DSpark is a completely different draft path and is the most informative next shot; if A starts but misses TPOT, DSpark is also the first thing to try.
B = h200-tp4-fp8-eagle.env LAST. It changes the weights themselves: 294.1 GB (nearly double the download and double the mirror rent) in exchange for DP-attention, which the FP4 path cannot have. Only worth that cost if both A and C fail for MoE-kernel/precision reasons.
This ordering, with the reason, is written into docs/RUNBOOK.md section 5 and cross-referenced from each recipe header.

=== DESIGN DECISIONS WORTH KNOWING ===
- run-staged.sh delegates to launch-bench-ec2.sh rather than duplicating launch logic, and enforces its OWN spend gate BEFORE invoking it. Case 15 asserts the launcher is never even called on refusal (the launcher's '渲染 user-data' banner must be absent), because otherwise the launcher's gate would mask a broken gate in run-staged.
- Stage cost data lives in run-staged.sh only as a FALLBACK price; the live price comes from `describe-spot-price-history --availability-zone` each run, degrading to the fallback with a warning. Measured this session: c5d.large $0.0295, g6e.xlarge $1.2082, p5en.48xlarge $26.6617.
- HONEST COST CORRECTION: the plan called gpu-smoke 'well under a dollar per hour'. g6e.xlarge spot in us-east-2a is currently $1.20/hr, so the 60-minute cap is ~$1.21 (a typical ~15-minute smoke is ~$0.30). The runbook states this discrepancy explicitly rather than repeating the plan's figure.
- The ledger is results/stage-ledger.json, already covered by the existing `results/*` gitignore rule, so it never enters git while still being a real file the next session can read. It records stage/run_id/instance_type/instance_id/started_at/ended_at/exit_status/s3_prefix/recipe/mode/note, is rewritten atomically via tempfile+os.replace, and tolerates a corrupt existing file by starting fresh rather than dying. Refusals are recorded too (exit_status 2), so 'which stages have been attempted' is answerable.
- --show-ledger renders one row per stage (latest attempt wins) using the same east_asian_width padding technique preflight.sh uses, because printf %-Ns misaligns CJK headers.
- collect-results.sh exits 1 when a benchmark misses threshold (matching run-benchmark.sh) but still writes both files; the fixture is tuned to PASS so the documented `collect && compare` one-liner works with &&.
- The fixture is explicitly labelled synthetic (`_fixture_synthetic: true` plus a Chinese `_fixture_note` in every file) and lives in tests/fixtures/, never results/. No fabricated measurement enters results/ or git.
- README edits are additive '✅ 2026-08-08 更正' / '➕ 新增' blocks next to the wrong text, in the existing Chinese style. Verified programmatically that section 12.1 (through 12.2) and section 6.1 (through 6.2) are byte-for-byte identical to HEAD, and 12.12's placeholder matrices are untouched.
- run-benchmark.sh remains the EKS path; the 4 changes are surgical (flag spelling, DP opt-in via empty DP_SIZE default + `--dp` now also flipping ENABLE_DP_ATTENTION, NVME_HOST_PATH variable with the README 9.1 note, JSONL-tolerant parsing). Guarded the JSON it emits: `"dp_size": ${DP_SIZE:-0}` so an unset DP_SIZE cannot produce invalid JSON.

Method identical to FEAT-002: copy scripts/+tests/ into .scratch/ (gitignored), apply one surgical patch, run the suite, confirm the target case flips to FAIL, delete the copy. Repo files were never left broken; .scratch/ was removed.
